issue.title: An SDD land phase cannot execute a "close the parent epic" deliverable, and nothing stops a plan from authoring one
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-fq.8.3 (epic sase-fq.8) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; independently verified by the sase-fq.8 land agent against the actual prompt sources.

THE DEFECT: an epic plan can author a phase whose deliverable is 'close the parent epic', and that phase can never complete it. Three independent mechanisms make it impossible:

1. The parent-close descendant guard. 'sase bead close <parent>' is rejected while any descendant is unclosed -- and the descendant doing the closing is itself unclosed at the moment it tries. Documented at sase/memory/sase_beads.md:91-93.
2. The phase-worker prompt (xprompt bd/work_phase_bead, src/sase/default_config.yml) and sase/memory/sase_beads.md:95 both tell phase workers never to close a parent epic; the land agent does that.
3. Only the land agent's prompt (xprompt bd/land_epic, src/sase/default_config.yml:950) actually carries the close-the-epic instruction, plus the symvision and plan-file-status steps that follow it.

So the phase's own guidance ('if the close is rejected, a phase bead is still open -- finish or reopen it instead') is circular: the still-open bead IS the phase attempting the close. The phase must either force the close, which its plan forbids, or leave its headline deliverable undone.

VERIFIED RECURRENCE -- four times, three different epics, in bead notes:
- sase-fq.8.3 ('Close out epic sase-fq'): could not close sase-fq because in_progress child epic sase-fq.8 existed; left it to sase-fq.8's land agent.
- sase-fr.9.3 ('Close epic sase-fr and retire its plan'): 'sase bead close sase-fr is rejected by the descendant-close guard because immediate parent epic sase-fr.9 ... is still open'.
- sase-fp.8.3 ('Land epic sase-fp'): 'functionally the land phase for the grandparent epic'.
- sase-bd.9.5 ('Close the epic'): 'I was instructed not to close my parent epic, so sase-bd closes once sase-bd.9 does'.
The pattern is specifically the child-epic shape: a follow-up epic is created under an epic to finish it, and the follow-up's land phase inherits 'close the grandparent' as a deliverable.

WHY IT MATTERS: every occurrence costs a landing round trip and leaves an epic in_progress after all its work is done, which is exactly the state that makes the next agent unsure whether the epic is finished. It also burns land-agent budget re-deriving why the close failed.

SCOPE -- pick one of two remediations:
A. Authoring side (cheapest). src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_plan.md says nothing about the land agent existing; it does not tell a plan author that closing the epic, running symvision, and marking the plan file done are the LAND agent's job and must not be authored as a phase. Add that rule, and consider a plan-validate check that rejects a phase whose description names closing its own parent or an ancestor epic. Note plan validation now lives in sase-core (see epic sase-g4), so the validation half is cross-repo; the skill-text half is local and is the minimum useful fix.
B. Tooling side. Give 'sase bead close' a deferred handoff -- 'close this ancestor once my own bead closes' -- so a phase can record the intent and the runtime executes it at the right moment. This also covers the child-epic chain (close sase-fq once sase-fq.8 closes) that today needs a human or a second land agent.

A alone stops new plans from being authored wrong; B alone makes the existing shape work. Doing A is recommended first because it is local and prevents recurrence; B is the larger change and should be sized on its own if triage wants it.

NOT CAUSED BY epic sase-fq/sase-fq.8: the mechanism predates it (sase-bd.9.5 hit it first) and is a property of the plan-authoring guidance and the bead-close guard, neither of which that epic touched.

payload.entry: Backlog triage 2026-08-06 (master 25285417d): NOT closed because it is invalid. The four recurrences cited (sase-fq.8.3, sase-fr.9.3, sase-fp.8.3, sase-bd.9.5) are documented in bead notes and the three blocking mechanisms are real. It lost its slot because every occurrence so far ended with the epic closed correctly by the next land agent or the owner — the cost is a landing round trip and an epic that reads in_progress for a while, not lost or corrupted state. Worth noting for whoever picks this up later: remediation A (teach src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_plan.md that closing the epic, running symvision, and marking the plan done are the LAND agent's job and must never be authored as a phase) is a local skill-text edit and would prevent recurrence on its own; remediation B (a deferred close handoff in 'sase bead close') is the larger change. If A is wanted as a standalone, it is small enough to just do rather than re-triage — but note that editing a bundled skill source is a memory-adjacent change that needs the owner's explicit go-ahead.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: real and recurring, but a land agent already absorbs the cost every time, so it is workflow friction rather than a defect that loses work. Cut for queue size.
